Describe gridded data without reading its values (experimental)

Source: R/proxy.R
as_proxy.Rd

as_proxy() describes one variable of gridded data and returns a SpatProxy. The data can be one netCDF file, a series of netCDF files, or a SpatVoxel already in memory. For a netCDF file it reads the metadata of the variable and its coordinates and applies the CF metadata once, so later steps can rely on each axis being in a fixed form. No values of the variable are read.

Usage

as_proxy(
  x,
  var = NULL,
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A netCDF file path or URL (e.g. OPeNDAP or NCZarr), several paths for a series of files, a connection opened with ncdf4::nc_open() (left open), or a SpatVoxel. var and the dimension arguments apply to files.

var

Name of the variable. NULL (the default) detects it when the file holds exactly one data variable.

lon_dim, lat_dim, depth_dim, time_dim

Names of the dimensions for each axis. NULL (the default) detects them from CF metadata (axis, standard_name, units) or common names.

Value

A SpatProxy.

Details

Besides one file, two sources give the same kind of proxy:

  • A series of files (several paths): the same variable on the same grid and depths in every file, each with its own dated time axis, such as one file per day. The files are put in time order and their time axes joined into one, in the first file's units. A series stops with an error when files repeat or overlap each other's time steps, when a file has no dated time axis, or when the files differ in grid (spatial tiles) or in the variable's units. The time axis keeps its bounds only when every file has them.

  • A SpatVoxel already in memory: one time step (the voxel's terra::time() when set), with the voxel's cells, depths and depth edges; a voxel without edges gets slabs halfway between its depths, as bounds = "midpoint" gives. The time must be a date or a date-time; a date is read as midnight UTC. A voxel whose time is a year, a month or a plain number stops with an error: give it a date-time, or remove its time with terra::time(v) <- NULL. as_voxel() returns the voxel itself.

For netCDF files, each axis is put in a fixed form:

  • Longitude and latitude: cell edges come from the coordinate's CF bounds variable, or halfway between neighbouring centres.

  • Depth: converted to metres positive down from the coordinate's units and positive attributes. Edges come from the CF bounds, or halfway between centres, cut at the surface and running half a gap below the deepest centre. A voxel read with as_voxel() keeps these edges. A depth axis stored deep to shallow is kept in that order and recorded as such.

  • Time: decoded with CFtime. Bounds are attached when the file has them; otherwise the axis has none (they aren't inferred). The time axis must be strictly increasing; a backwards or out-of-order axis is an error that suggests sorting the file, for example with CDO's sorttimestamp. Only the standard, gregorian and proleptic_gregorian calendars are supported. A climatological time axis with one step, such as a World Ocean Atlas period, is recorded as a climatology without a date; climatologies with more steps aren't supported yet.

  • CRS: EPSG:4326, unless the variable's grid_mapping gives another geographic CRS as WKT (crs_wkt or spatial_ref).

Regular longitude-latitude grids with coordinate values are supported; curvilinear, projected and rotated-pole grids are rejected. Bad cell bounds (cells that don't contain their centre, have no width or overlap) stop with an error, and so does a variable with no values along a dimension (for example an unlimited time dimension with no records).

Experimental

SpatProxy and as_proxy() are experimental. Their slots and behaviour may change without notice while the core object is built.

See also

SpatProxy

Examples

x <- as_proxy(system.file("extdata", "example_3d.nc", package = "ocean3d"))
x
#> class      : SpatProxy (experimental)
#> source     : example_3d.nc
#> variable   : temp (degrees_C)
#> dimensions : 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 (lon x lat x depth x time)
#> lon        : 0 to 1, 2 cells, edges inferred
#> lat        : 40 to 41, 2 cells, edges inferred
#> depth      : 0 to 100 m, 3 levels, shallow first, edges inferred
#> time       : 2020-01-01 to 2020-01-06, 3 steps, standard calendar, no bounds
#> crs        : EPSG:4326

# Each axis in its fixed form: depth in metres, time as a CFtime object.
x@axes$depth$centres
#> [1]   0  50 100
x@axes$time$cftime
#> CF calendar:
#>   Origin  : 2020-01-01T00:00:00
#>   Units   : days
#>   Type    : standard
#> 
#> Time series:
#>   Elements: [2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-06] (average of 2.500000 days between 3 elements)
#>   Bounds  : not set

# Read one time step into memory as a SpatVoxel.
v <- as_voxel(x, time = 1)
depths(v)
#> [1]   0  50 100
